# Marking what Imprimatur set up for you

Imprimatur looks at everything configured in your project, such as installed plugins, instructions, tools and automated checks, and tells you which of those it set up itself. This way you can tell at a glance what came from Imprimatur and what you or your team added yourselves.

## Contents

- [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)
- [Words used here](#words-used-here)

## What it does for you

- Shows a clear label next to anything Imprimatur created or installed, so you don't mistake it for your own setup.
- Covers all the different kinds of setup: installed add-ons, instructions, tools and automated checks.
- Leaves everything else unlabelled, so you can see your own work clearly.
- Keeps Imprimatur's internal data out of the list entirely, so it doesn't clutter the view.

## How it works

1. You open the view that lists everything set up in your project.
2. Imprimatur checks each item against a set of rules to decide if it made that item.
3. If it recognises its own work, it adds "Imprimatur" to the start of that item's description.
4. Items that mix Imprimatur's work with your own are only labelled on the specific parts that are Imprimatur's.
5. Imprimatur's own internal files are left out of the list, since they are not part of your setup.

## Good to know

- If Imprimatur does not recognise something as its own, it simply leaves it unlabelled. This does not cause any other problem.
- The label is only shown in this view. It is not used anywhere else in the product.

## Words used here

- hook: Imprimatur scripts that run automatically during a session to record edits, collect pending items, and run checks.
- Imprimatur: the product's name. A tool that shows an agent's edits as tracked changes until you approve them.
- session: one working session with the agent.
